qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: German secondary residential rental portfolio faces strict statutory rent controls (Mietpreisbremse and municipal Mietspiegel caps) that restrict pricing power below inflation. Multi-year unlevered ROIC sits structurally at 2-4%, far below the 12% threshold. Local property management clustering provides marginal administrative overhead savings but no structural pricing advantage.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (G3 Moat & Pricing). German secondary residential landlord subject to statutory rent controls (Mietpreisbremse, Mietspiegel) that cap rent increases. Unlevered capital returns (ROIC 2-4%) structurally fall far short of the 12% hurdle rate.
qualitative.evidence: TAG Immobilien manages ~85k residential rental units across northern and eastern Germany alongside Polish residential development/rental operations (ROBYG and Resi4Rent). Multi-year GAAP ROIC hovers around 2-4%, constrained by low gross rental yields and strict statutory rent caps in Germany. High debt leverage (€4.2B+ debt, LTV ~45%) is required to generate single-digit equity returns, failing the Munger standard for an enduring high-return moat.
